correctness.rationale: On the Grassmann chart at the common-kernel plane, expanding \(\det M(x,y,z)\) gives ten cubic coefficient equations. Three solve with unit coefficients for the graph coordinates \(a_3,b_3,c_3\). After the submitted polynomial coordinate change, the remaining ideal is generated by \(A^2,AH,H^2+2AK,AC-HK,2CH-K^2,CK,C^2\) and is independent of the two reduced-component coordinates. The reduced Gröbner basis stated in the package is algebraically consistent with the displayed transverse generators; the inspected exact-commit verifier implements the full determinant-to-ideal transformation and all cubic reductions. The eight standard monomials \(1,A,H,K,C,H^2,HK,K^2\) give Hilbert function \((1,4,3)\), length eight and maximal-ideal cube zero. Mokhtar's Example 6.26 states that the reduced common-kernel component is a single \(\mathrm{GL}_3\)-orbit; equivariance transports this local chart type to every point, so the generic transverse length is the scheme-theoretic multiplicity.
